f.title: Designate a QPPV with defined functions
f.statement: The MAH must designate a pharmacovigilance officer (QPPV) who shall maintain an effective PV system; ensure conduct of PV and submission of all PV documents per legal requirements; have an overview of safety profiles and emerging safety concerns; act as single contact point during inspection and monitoring and respond promptly to FDA requests; and maintain and update the company database of all adverse reactions with all reported cases on file.
f.clause: V.A The Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance

rows.quote:
The MAH must designate a pharmacovigilance officer which also refers to as
Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) who shall assume the following
functions:
e maintain an effective Pharmacovigilance system of the MAH
e ensure conduct of pharmacovigilance and submission of all
pharmacovigilance-related documents in accordance with legal
requirements
e havean overview of the safety profiles and any emerging safety concerns in
relation to the products for which the MAH holds authorizations
e actas a single contact point during inspection and monitoring and respond
promptly for any request/inquiry from FDA
e maintain and update company database of all adverse reactions involving
their products and have on file all reported cases
rows.location: V.A The Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.clause: V.A The Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance

f.statement: A valid serious ADR report must provide the minimum mandatory information: one identifiable patient (at least one of initials, medical record number, date of birth, age, age group, gestation period or gender); one or more suspected adverse reactions; one or more suspected products (interacting products also considered suspected); and one or more identifiable reporters (qualification, name, initials or address). A case lacking any of the four elements is incomplete and does not qualify for submission.

f.title: Submit follow-up reports within 15 calendar days citing the initial DTN
f.statement: When additional medically significant information is received, the MAH must submit a follow-up report as soon as possible and no later than 15 calendar days after receipt, labelled as follow-up, cross-referenced to the previous report and stating the DTN of the initial submission.

f.statement: Overseas cases reported locally where the patient is Filipino and the product was obtained in the Philippines should be treated as local cases; only serious ones are reportable and the country of occurrence should be stated. Other foreign ADRs are not reportable unless requested.

rows.quote:
For cases that occurred overseas and reported locally, when information is
available that the patient is Filipino and the product is obtained from the
Philippines, the case should be treated as a local case. However, only the
serious adverse reaction qualifies reporting to FDA. The country of
occurrence should also be stated.
Any adverse reactions occurring outside the Philippines other than the
conditions above does not qualify for reporting to FDA, unless otherwise,
requested.

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Report lack of efficacy with adverse outcome using clinical judgement
f.statement: Lack of efficacy is reportable when the product fails to produce the expected benefit and results in an adverse outcome (e.g. critical conditions, life-threatening disease, vaccines, contraceptives); clinical judgement should be applied, e.g. a newly resistant strain in a life-threatening infection should be submitted within 15 days, while inappropriate use should not.
f.clause: V.C Reporting of Adverse Reaction 3.e Reports of Lack of Efficacy

rows.quote:
Lack of efficacy is reportable when the product fails to produce expected
pharmacologic or therapeutic benefit and results in an adverse outcome
including worsening of the condition of the patient. Products used in critical
conditions or for the treatment of life-threatening disease, vaccines,
contraceptives are examples of such cases.
Clinical judgement should be considered to qualify the report of lack of
efficacy. For example, a report of lack of efficacy with an antibiotic used in a
life-threatening situation where the use of the product was not in fact
appropriate for the infective agent should not be submitted. However, a report
of lack of efficacy for a life-threatening infection, which appears to be due to
the development of a newly resistant strain of a bacterium previously
regarded as susceptible, should be submitted within 15 days.
rows.location: V.C Reporting of Adverse Reaction 3.e Reports of Lack of Efficacy
rows.review_note: Review: 15 days stated in the example; clock start taken from section C.1 and unit assumed calendar days as in C.1. Double-check: confidence lowered for inferred clock wording.

f.title: Follow up pregnancy and paternal exposures; report abnormal outcomes
f.statement: Maternal or paternal exposure must be followed up and reported only when it results in an abnormal outcome (e.g. congenital anomaly, malformation) as a parent-child report; where both parent and child/fetus have suspected ADRs, two linked reports should be submitted. Exposure without an adverse reaction is not reportable.
f.clause: V.C Reporting of Adverse Reaction 3.i Outcomes of Use during Pregnancy

rows.quote:
The outcome of report of product administration or product that was taken by
pregnant woman or a case of paternal exposure must be followed up and
reported only when it resulted to an abnormal outcome, i.e. congenital
anomaly, malformations, etc. This case is referred to as a parent-child report.
When both the parent and exposed child or fetus experience suspected
adverse reactions, two separate reports should be submitted but linked to each
other.
Maternal or paternal exposure to drug products without adverse reaction does
not qualify for reporting to FDA.
rows.location: V.C Reporting of Adverse Reaction 3.i Outcomes of Use during Pregnancy
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Screen company-managed websites and social media for ADRs
f.statement: MAHs should regularly screen websites and social media under their management or responsibility for potential ADR reports; cases should be verified that patient and reporter exist, and are non-valid until verified directly with the patient, the patient's HCP or a reporter with direct contact.

rows.quote:
MAHs should regularly screen websites including social media under their
management or responsibility for potential adverse reaction case reports on
the use of their product. The case should be verified that the patient and
reporter really exist. The report should be considered non-valid until it can be
verified directly with the patient, the patient’s healthcare professional or a
reporter who had direct contact with the patient.

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

reported to FDA. A copy of the column or paper (with title and date of issue)

f.clause: V.E Risk Management Plan, Philippine-specific Annex
f.exceptions: Annex may be omitted if the GVP Module V-compliant RMP is made or intended for the Philippine market.

rows.quote: The latest template of the Philippine-specific Annex available in the FDA website must be used.
rows.location: V.E Risk Management Plan, Philippine-specific Annex
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Submit updated RMP on significant change or FDA request
f.statement: An updated RMP is submitted whenever there is a significant change (new information changing benefit-risk, a milestone reached or activity terminated/added/altered, changes to safety concerns) or upon FDA request.
f.clause: V.E Risk Management Plan, Philippine-specific Annex

rows.quote:
Updated RMP is submitted only on the following conditions:
e whenever there is a significant change to the RMP, including but not
limited to:
o when the RMP is modified as a result of new information that
may lead to a change to the benefit-risk profile;
o when an important (vigilance or risk minimization) milestone is
reached, or an activity is terminated, added, or substantially
altered;
o when changes to the summary of ongoing safety concerns are
made.
e upon request of FDA;
rows.location: V.E Risk Management Plan, Philippine-specific Annex
rows.review_note: Review: descriptive "is submitted" read as the trigger for a duty. Double-check: agreed, confidence 85.

f.title: Conduct routine PV locally for all registered products
f.statement: Routine pharmacovigilance should be conducted locally for all registered drugs and biologicals, including systems for collection and recording of all suspected ADRs, submission to FDA, signal detection, significant safety information updates and actions by other regulators.
f.clause: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan
f.processes: Signal detection; Safety intake & collection; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote:
Routine pharmacovigilance should be conducted locally for all registered drugs
and biological products for human use. It includes activities as required in this
Circular such as systems and processes that ensure collection and recording of
all suspected adverse reactions, submission of reports to FDA, signal detection,
updates of significant safety information and actions taken by other regulatory
agencies.
rows.location: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Design PV plan studies relevant, feasible and non-promotional
f.statement: Studies in the PV plan should relate to safety concerns in the safety specification, be feasible and not include any promotional element; FDA may require local Category 3 studies for specific concerns in the Filipino population.
f.clause: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: They should relate to the safety concerns identified in the safety specification, be feasible and should not include any element of a promotional nature.
rows.location: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Submit local non-interventional PASS protocol with the Annex
f.statement: For a locally conducted non-interventional PASS, the protocol (per GVP Module VIII B.3.1) should be attached to the Philippine-specific Annex and ADRs reported per this Circular; interventional local PASS follow clinical trial rules.
f.clause: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan

rows.quote:
If a PASS is non-interventional, to be conducted locally, the protocol following
the latest EMA/813938/2011 GVP Module VIII Section B.3.1. Format and
content of the study protocol should be submitted as attachment to RMP
Philippine-Specific Annex. Adverse reactions should be reported to FDA in
accordance with the provisions of Reporting of Adverse Reactions of this
Circular.
rows.location: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Submit PASS final study report within 12 months of end of data collection
f.statement: The final PASS study report, following GVP Module VIII B.4.3.2 format, should be submitted within 12 months of the end of data collection.
f.clause: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan

rows.deadline: Within 12 months of end of data collection
rows.quote: The final study report, following the format of GVP Module VIII Section B.4.3.2. should be submitted within 12 months of the end of data collection.
rows.location: V.E.4 Pharmacovigilance Plan
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Submit PBRERs on FDA request within 70/90 days of DLP
f.statement: When required by FDA, PBRERs covering up to 12 months are submitted within 70 calendar days, and those covering more than 12 months within 90 calendar days, from the FDA-set data lock point.
f.clause: V.F.1 PBRER Reporting Requirements

rows.deadline: 70 calendar days (<=12 months) / 90 calendar days (>12 months) from DLP
rows.quote:
Whenever required by the FDA - (a) covering up to 12 months: submitted
within 70 calendar days; and (b) covering more than 12 months: submitted
within 90 calendar days from the data lock point set by the FDA
rows.location: V.F.1 PBRER Reporting Requirements
rows.review_note: Review: one rule row records the 70-day limit; the 90-day limit is in the free text. Double-check: should be split into two rows when re-cut.

deadline_rule.applies_to: PBRERs covering up to 12 months (90 days if longer)

f.title: Submit PBRERs for new drugs and biologicals 6-monthly for 2 years, then annually for 3
f.statement: For new drug products (new active substance) and biological products, PBRERs are submitted at 6-month intervals for 2 years from local registration or international birth date, then annually for 3 years; PBRERs are also submitted with variation applications they support. Format follows ICH E2C.
f.clause: V.F.1 PBRER Reporting Requirements
f.applicability: New drug products with new active substance; biological products

rows.quote:
New Drug Products (applicable only to pharmaceutical products with new
active substance that has not been previously registered in the Philippines)
& Biological Products (a) for initial period of 2 years at 6 months interval
either from the date of local registration of the product or its international
birthdate; and (b) annually for the next 3 years
rows.location: V.F.1 PBRER Reporting Requirements
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Notify FDA of foreign regulatory actions within 72 hours
f.statement: Regulatory actions by other national authorities that may influence the benefit-risk profile (withdrawal, recall/defects, indication removal, failed renewal for safety, safety DHPC) must be communicated to the FDA-CDRR Pharmacovigilance Section as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after receipt of information.
f.clause: V.G Update of Actions Taken by Other National Drug Regulatory Agencies

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 72 hours after receipt of information
rows.quote:
Regulatory actions taken by other national drug regulatory authorities which may
influence the overall benefit-risk profile of the product must be communicated to
the Pharmacovigilance Section, FDA-CDRR, PRSDD as soon as possible but not
later than 72 hours after the receipt of information.
rows.location: V.G Update of Actions Taken by Other National Drug Regulatory Agencies
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Regulatory actions by other national authorities

f.title: Disseminate DHPCs for safety issues; submit copy to FDA beforehand with reporting statement
f.statement: Dissemination of a DHPC letter is required whenever there are related safety issues, either on MAH initiative or as FDA requires (joint letters possible). A copy must be submitted to FDA before dissemination, and the letter should include the FDA online/email ADR reporting statement.
f.clause: V.G Update of Actions Taken by Other National Drug Regulatory Agencies

rows.quote:
Dissemination of Direct Healthcare Professional Communication Letter is required
whenever there are related safety issues on the product, as appropriate. It may
either be an initiative of the MAH or as required by FDA as necessary. In certain
circumstances, a joint DHCP letter among MAHs may be required as appropriate.
A copy of the DHCP letter prior to dissemination should be submitted to notify the
FDA.
rows.location: V.G Update of Actions Taken by Other National Drug Regulatory Agencies
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: MAH retains ultimate responsibility when outsourcing PV
f.statement: The MAH may transfer any or all PV tasks, including the PV role, to another person or organisation, but ultimate responsibility for fulfilment, quality and integrity of all PV obligations always resides with the MAH.
f.clause: V.H Outsourcing of Pharmacovigilance Activities

rows.quote: The MAH may transfer any or all of the pharmacovigilance task and functions, including the role of pharmacovigilance, to another person(s) or organization, but the ultimate responsibility for the fulfillment of all pharmacovigilance obligations and its quality and integrity always resides with the MAH.
rows.location: V.H Outsourcing of Pharmacovigilance Activities
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote, level and statement agree.

f.title: Be ready for announced or unannounced PV inspections
f.statement: MAHs and PV service providers are subject to FDA assessments, audits and inspections of compliance with PV obligations, generally on notice, but FDA may inspect unannounced.
f.clause: V.I Pharmacovigilance Inspections
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote:
To determine and ensure that a functional pharmacovigilance system is in place in
all MAHs or any person or organization providing pharmacovigilance activities
(outsourcing) to MAH, assessment and audits on compliance to pharmacovigilance
obligations shall be conducted. The conduct of pharmacovigilance inspection will
generally be upon notice; however, the FDA reserves the right to conduct
unannounced inspection, if necessary.
rows.location: V.I Pharmacovigilance Inspections
rows.review_note: Review: duty is to be subject to inspection (authority power). Double-check: kept for inspection readiness.

dates.title: FDA Circular 2020-003: MAHs ICH-E2B compliant by end of 2025
dates.quote: All MAHSs should be ICH-E2B compliant before the end of Year 2025.
